plan.statusSummary: Batch regressed at the generation stage across all 3 tasks, so there is no new empirical signal from backtests. The mutation brief is also internally inconsistent across tasks: tasks 1-2 say recover tradability by loosening entry gating only, while task 3 says prioritize exits/risk before entry expansion. Existing knowledge already covers regime-aware exits, counter-trend blocking, drawdown control, and trade-count recovery, so the main unmet need is not generic ideas but compact, implementation-safe patterns for single-block mutations that preserve trade count and avoid generation failure. Refresh should target low-complexity Pine design patterns for localized entry/exit changes under trend_down/range conditions and tradability-preserving drawdown controls.
knowledgeGaps: Implementation-safe single-block Pine mutation patterns that reduce generation failures when adding localized regime-aware logic.
Minimal-complexity trend_down long-taper or confirmation rules that preserve trade count better than full regime blocks.
Localized loser-exit and time-stop patterns for range/range_squeeze that are simple enough to express without multi-subsystem rewrites.
Low-trade-count recovery methods after exit tightening that rely on selective re-entry or narrower regime application with minimal code footprint.
Conflict-resolution guidance for sequencing repairs when objectives alternate between entry-gating recovery and exit-tightening drawdown control.
searchQueries: What simple Pine Script patterns implement a single localized regime-aware long filter or position-size taper in downtrends without collapsing trade count?
What low-complexity exit rules for range or volatility-compression regimes improve adverse excursion and drawdown while preserving trade frequency in medium-horizon index strategies?
plan.paperQuestion: Which simple, single-block strategy modifications most reliably improve drawdown control or counter-trend exposure in medium-horizon equity index systems without materially reducing trade count, especially via asymmetric trend_down entry confirmation, partial risk tapering, time-based loser exits, or selective re-entry after tighter exits?
plan.ingestionTitle: Low-complexity regime-aware mutation patterns for drawdown control and trade-count preservation
